approaches_tried.reason: bash's ${var:-{}} parameter expansion mishandles a literal {} default value, silently appending an extra trailing } to the output whenever var is non-empty (confirmed via isolated bash -c repro) -- caused '1\n0' style corrupted values and an arithmetic syntax error. Fixed by using ${var:-null} instead, which jq's // operators handle cleanly.
